title: Cracks in the Foundation: A Civil Infrastructure Dataset to Challenge Vision Foundation Models
mechanism: 150k-tile infrastructure defect benchmark comparing EoMT (DINOv2/DINOv3), Mask DINO, YOLO and RF-DETR under one protocol.
adaptation: Evidence that VFM mask classifiers do not fix thin-crack masks alone: keep a per-pixel crack head; in our benchmark report crack with tolerant metrics (relF1@2) beside strict IoU.
min_experiment: No separate run; its finding is tested by the EoMT arm's crack IoU vs relF1@2 gap compared with the house model.
evidence: R: tiled 1024: EoMT DINOv3 mask mAP 24.2 overall (best), crack mask mAP 4.7 (DINOv3) / 5.0 (DINOv2) vs YOLOv11-xl 8.6; authors: mask mAP plunges to single digits for cracks. Data on HF ibm-research/cif-dataset.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark design: add zero-shot FM rows, test centre bias (crack position within cell), possibly use as extra crack pretraining data (different modality).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Benchmark-only: report zero-shot SAM3 / SAM2 rows and a centre-bias analysis; no training needed.

alt_notes.adaptation: Benchmark lesson: report zero-shot and in-context FM rows beside supervised rows with tolerant crack metrics; possible crack-shape pretraining data (HF ibm-research/cif-dataset), overlaps D36.
alt_notes.min_experiment: No score experiment; include FM zero-shot/in-context rows in the benchmark table.
